calls.headline: The pound hits a one-year high as foreigners buy bills and remittances surge
calls.body: The central bank's dollar rate fell 66 piasters on Tuesday to EGP 53.39, a 1.2% gain for the pound and its strongest level in the data log's past year; it was above 56 on October 29. Foreigners made net purchases of about $567m of government debt on the secondary market on Monday, $577.6m of it in treasury bills, according to Al-Ain, citing exchange data; Middle East Observer, citing Hapi Journal, puts foreign and Arab buying at $614.7m. Remittances reached $13bn in July–September, up 20.4%, and a record $38.2bn for nine months (central bank via EnterpriseAM). The dollar index rose 0.53% to 102.22 the same day, so the move was local.
calls.view: Hot money is coming back for 26% bills against 12.7% inflation, and record remittances give the pound a second, steadier support; together they keep the dollar in the EGP 52–55 range into the IMF program's December 15 expiry. The risk is timing: a Fed hike on December 9, now fully priced, comes eight days before the central bank meets and could slow the inflows. Banks gain most, from cheaper dollar funding and fee income; importers' margins widen.
calls.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 55.50 (central bank sell rate) before December 9.

calls.headline: EGX30 jumps 2.08% on a year's busiest turnover; foreigners turn buyers
calls.line: Foreign money returned to equities, if modestly, the day after selling EGP 303m.
calls.body: The EGX30 rose 2.08% to 52,483.46 on Tuesday on EGP 12.8bn of turnover across about 325,500 trades (Al Mal), the busiest session in the data log's past year, and closed back above its 50-day average of about 52,385. Foreigners bought a net EGP 42.1m and Egyptians EGP 14.3m while Arabs sold EGP 56.4m (Masrawy, Al Mal); Egyptians made up 90.6% of trading (Alborsa). EFG Holding rose 6.8% to EGP 25.61 and the EGX70 EWI 2.99%, its sixth straight gain.
calls.view: Breadth and turnover say local investors are fully back after October's margin calls, and the small foreign buying ends three sessions of selling; with foreigners also buying bills, the desk expects the index to hold above 50,000 into Telecom Egypt's results and to test the 53,000s by month-end. EFG is the cleanest way to own the turnover.
calls.wrong: The EGX30 closes below 50,000 before the end of November.

calls.headline: Juhayna's profit jumps 60%; Banque du Caire's rises 4.7%
calls.line: Results season is rewarding consumer names that raised prices more than the banks.
calls.body: Juhayna's nine-month consolidated profit rose 60% to EGP 2.04bn from EGP 1.27bn, on sales up 25% to EGP 27.66bn (Mubasher, from the disclosure). Banque du Caire's consolidated profit attributable to shareholders rose 4.7% to EGP 13.11bn, with net interest income up 10.4% to EGP 28.45bn (Arab Finance). Eastern Company's nine-month profit rose to EGP 8.99bn from EGP 6.48bn, with the third quarter more than doubling to EGP 4.83bn, according to one outlet (Youlyou). Banque du Caire rose 4.8% to EGP 5.86; Juhayna 0.2% to EGP 24.95.
calls.view: Juhayna's figures show price rises of 4–11% stuck without losing volume, and a firmer pound now cheapens its imported inputs: the desk projects a move toward its 52-week high. Banque du Caire grew far slower than CIB's 18% underlying rate, so its rise looks like post-listing demand rather than earnings; the desk does not chase it.
calls.wrong: Juhayna closes below EGP 22 before the end of January.
calls.notice: Eastern Company's figures are reported by one outlet and not yet confirmed; the view does not rely on them.

calls.headline: Suez container traffic runs 36% above last year, IMF PortWatch shows
calls.line: The canal's dollar income keeps recovering, a support for the pound and port stocks.
calls.body: Container ships averaged 13.5 Suez transits a day in the four weeks to November 8, against 9.9 a year earlier, and cargo capacity through the canal rose 18.7% to about 1.85m metric tons a day, while all transits rose 2.9% to 43.3 a day (IMF PortWatch). A Liberia-flagged tanker was attacked in the Gulf on Tuesday, a day after an Adnoc-operated ship was damaged (The National), and Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh (Al Jazeera). Alexandria Containers closed at EGP 33.00, against Naeem's EGP 33.6 target.
calls.view: The return of large container ships is lifting revenue per transit, the reason canal receipts nearly doubled in October; that dollar income is steadier than portfolio flows. The Houthis are firing at Saudi targets, not at Red Sea shipping, which is what keeps the recovery going; a turn back to ships is the risk.
calls.wrong: Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping resume, or Alexandria Containers closes below EGP 29.

calls.headline: Hot October CPI locks in a December hike; two-year yield jumps 17bp
calls.body: Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October against 0.3% expected and core prices 0.3% against 0.2%, with shelter more than 30% of the rise (BLS via CNBC); no annual rate was published because the 2025 shutdown left no October base. Futures now fully price a quarter-point hike on December 9 and about 14% odds of a half point (CME FedWatch via CNBC), after Governor Waller said that a core reading near 0.3% would mean "a stronger policy move may be needed" (Federal Reserve). The two-year yield rose 17 basis points and the 10-year closed at 4.98% (Treasury). The S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq 0.74%.
calls.view: A hike is now in the price, so the next leg depends on whether the Fed goes 50 or signals more in 2027. That keeps pressure on the most expensive growth stocks and favors companies returning cash now, such as Costco and Berkshire. The desk expects the 10-year to hold between 4.8% and 5.2% into the meeting and the S&P 500 to trade sideways, not to break down.
calls.wrong: The S&P 500 closes below 7,250, about 3.6% lower, before December 9.

calls.headline: Nvidia slides 5.5% to a March low; Broadcom gains 3.9%
calls.line: Investors keep buying AI hardware but not the stock with key-person risk.
calls.body: Nvidia fell 5.5% to $168.89 on Tuesday, its lowest close since March and about 30% below its October record, as the board's inquiry into Jensen Huang's ties to a woman suspected of spying for China continued (CBS News). Broadcom rose 3.9% to $331.98 after Anthropic's amended filing named it a roughly $1bn buyer in a $26bn private placement at the IPO price (GuruFocus via Yahoo Finance); Nvidia and Google are reported to take $10bn each. Goldman Sachs called chip stocks oversold. Results are due November 17.
calls.view: The selling is about governance, not demand, which is why Broadcom gained the same day; it caps Nvidia until the inquiry ends or results reassure. The desk's chip view, judged Friday, stands with Nvidia far below $220. A clean report on November 17 could spark a sharp rebound from 22% below the 50-day average, so the desk does not add to the bearish call.
calls.wrong: Nvidia closes above $200 before its results on November 17.

calls.headline: Anthropic seeks up to $64.4bn; Microsoft falls 2.2% on its office tools
calls.line: The biggest AI listing yet both lifts its backers' stakes and threatens software incumbents.
calls.body: Anthropic set a range of $70–78 for 825 million shares, raising up to $64.4bn at a valuation of up to $1.4tn, with trading expected around November 19 (CNBC). Alongside it, AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC agreed to buy $26bn of non-voting shares at the IPO price. Microsoft fell 2.2% to $533.16 after Anthropic unveiled workplace tools including Claude Sheets, a rival to Excel (FXLeaders); Amazon, an early backer, rose 1.5% to $270.87.
calls.view: The raise will pull money from other AI names in the week it prices, and Anthropic's move into office software is a real, if slow, threat to Microsoft's most profitable franchise. Amazon and Google gain a marked-up stake. The desk sees Microsoft lagging the Nasdaq into the listing.
calls.wrong: Microsoft closes above $560, its record area, before November 20.

calls.headline: Costco declares a $30 special dividend and a new $4bn buyback
calls.line: Cash returned now is what a hiking Fed rewards.
calls.body: Costco's board declared a $30-a-share special dividend, about $13.3bn, payable December 4 to holders of record November 24, and approved a $4bn buyback running to November 2030, replacing a program under which $3.1bn had been bought (company filing). Costco closed flat at $1,066.14, about 3% below its 52-week high of $1,094.32. Berkshire Hathaway's B shares rose 1.4% to a record $583.34.
calls.view: The payout is about 2.8% of the share price and returns cash the market had expected, so the stock may slip by the dividend on the record date rather than rise. The bigger point is the rotation: steady earners that return cash keep outperforming AI spenders while rates rise, which supports the desk's open rotation view.
calls.wrong: Costco closes below $1,000 before the end of November, excluding the dividend.

news.headline: Bernstein: Oracle 18 months from positive free cash flow
news.text: It reiterated outperform and a $325 target; Oracle fell 1.5% to $117.98.

global.finding: Brent settled 1.2% lower at $91.49 on Tuesday after briefly dipping below $90 on hopes of an end to the Iran war, then traded near $92 on Wednesday after a tanker attack in the Gulf; gold fell 2.0% to about $4,030 as US yields rose and the dollar index climbed 0.5% to 102.22.

notes.brent: Egypt imports fuel and LNG, so Brent at $91.49, down from about $98 on Friday, trims the import bill; spot LNG stays dear, which is why industry is still rationed.
notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold: the 24K gram fell to EGP 7,030 from 7,175 as gold dropped 2.0% and the pound firmed.
notes.dxy: At 102.22, within 0.4% of its 52-week high after the hot US inflation print; a stronger dollar usually slows money into emerging markets, though the pound rose the same day.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite: about $73,800 on Wednesday, below its 200-day average and down about 15% this year.

news.headline: Tanker attacked near Hormuz; four Indian crew injured
news.text: A Liberia-flagged oil tanker was hit a day after an Adnoc-operated ship was damaged; Iran denies talks with Washington.

news.headline: Brent briefly dips below $90 on Iran peace hopes
news.text: It settled 1.2% lower at $91.49, the first dip under $90 since August.

news.headline: Fed's Waller: a stronger move may be needed
news.text: He said a core CPI reading near 0.3% would argue for more than a quarter-point hike; it came in at 0.3%.

news.headline: Suez container transits run 36% above last year
news.text: 13.5 a day in the four weeks to November 8 against 9.9; cargo capacity up 18.7%.

news.headline: China's trade surplus tops $1tn for a second year
news.text: October exports jumped 35.2% and imports 41.6%, led by chips and AI hardware.
